lens: Every number printed in the journal article and its display items, re-derived from the committed artifact or module that produces it — counts, fractions, percentages, denominators, totals, and every figure that appears in more than one place. Check that each derived total is DERIVED and not typed, and that two statements of the same quantity agree. Run the producing modules rather than reading their recorded outputs.
what_i_read: research/modalities/junction-aso-offtarget-*.json (all 38 default-depth and 38 deep 5-6-5 screens, enumerated programmatically)
research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md (passages on censoring and the deeper pass only)
central_claim: Two junction-spanning 5-6-5 gapmers — one at EWSR1 exon 12 and one at TAF15 exon 6, both to NR4A3 exon 3 — are named as synthesis-ready research reagents with screened scramble controls and a pre-registrable knockdown design, on the basis of a five-screen in-silico specificity panel over 190 designs at 38 in-frame junctions whose central finding is that the wild-type parent liability is large (87 of 190), is not distinguishable from what any two exon termini of these genes would give, and turns on an adopted ten-base-pair convention.

p1s.summary: The censoring bound the paper puts in front of every clean-design count is measured on the DEFAULT-depth alignment screen (7 failures, 47 of 183 assessable), but the paper's only clean-design count — 'Three designs clear every screen' — is computed on the DEEP screens, which have a different set of three failures and no censoring at all. Worse, one of the three named clean designs is itself one of the seven the paper says 'never returned'.
p1s.evidence: Re-derived by enumerating the 38 default-depth 5-6-5 screens research/modalities/junction-aso-offtarget-<junction>.json: 190 design rows, status counts {screened: 183, screen_failed: 7}, and 47 of the 183 screened rows carry a stored hit list at least as long as their reported near-match count (uncensored). Both figures reproduce the manuscript exactly, so the numbers themselves are right for that tier. The seven failures are AGGGCATATCACCAGG / GCATATCACCAGGCTT / CAGGGCATATCACCAG at EWSR1_e9, CAGGGCATATTGTTCT at FUS_e3, GGGCATATCTCGCCGC at TAF15_e12, GGGCATATCAAGCGCT at TCF12_e7, and GGCATATCTTGCATAA at TCF12_e9. Enumerating the 38 deep (deep500/clean9) 5-6-5 screens gives a different picture: 190 rows, {screened: 187, screen_failed: 3} — the three being CAGGGCATATCTCCAC and GCATATCTCCACCTCC at FUS_e5 and AGGGCATATCTTCATC at TFG_e2 — and all 187 hit lists are complete (0 censored). research/modalities/aso-per-junction-table.json, which joins the five screens at the deep tier, holds 187 design rows and names those same three as 'designs_absent_because_the_deep_screen_did_not_return'. Filtering that table for designs with no hybridisable near-match, no precursor gap-paired hit, no genome named-target site and a mature-parent duplex below ten base pairs returns exactly the paper's three: AGGGCATATCGGAGTC at FUS_e8 (parent duplex 0), GGGCATATCCGACATG at TAF15_e1 (0) and GGGCATATCAAGCGCT at TCF12_e7 (8 bp, wild-type NR4A3) — so the count of three is correct, and it rests on 187 assessable records, not on 47 of 183. GGGCATATCAAGCGCT appears in both lists: it is the sixth of the seven default-screen failures AND one of the three designs the paper reports as clearing every screen. The companion extended report states the reconciliation the journal article omits (research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:509-515: 'Seven of the 190 designs had failed at the remote service and carried no count at all … all seven returned at the deeper ceiling, six of them dirty and one (5'-GGGCATATCAAGCGCT-3' at TCF12 exon 7) with three near-matches and none on the sense strand'), so within the journal article alone 'never returned' is unqualified and contradicted by the paper's own candidate list. The defect is presentational, not arithmetic: the three deep-tier failures are all independently condemned by the mature-parent screen (12 bp against NR4A3, 10 bp against TAF15 and 11 bp against NR4A3 respectively, from research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json), so none of them could have been a fourth clean design and the value three is exact rather than a floor.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The fix is to say which tier each denominator belongs to — 'seven of the 190 default-ceiling alignment screens never returned' and 'the deeper pass returned 187 of 190 with every hit list complete, and decided six of the seven' — not to change any number. The silent-regression risk is the opposite edit: dropping 'default' from the second bound's 'most designs clean at the default search ceiling', or re-tiering the clean count to the default screens (where the same filter returns nine, not three, per the submission plan's 'Nine designs at six junctions carry no hybridisable near-match'), would silently swap the denominator under a sentence that reads unchanged. Nothing in the repository binds the tier of the 7/183/47 triple to the tier of the clean count: they are computed by different modules over different screen files, and the guard that pins the censoring derivation is scoped to the extended report alone (noted at research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-guard-coverage-audit.md:184), so the journal article's copy is unmeasured.
p1s.where: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md:196-201 (the two bounds) against :222-224 (the three clean designs)

p2s.summary: '8 designs carry a fully paired sixteen-base-pair off-target duplex and 45 one inside 2 kcal/mol of their own' coordinates two counts of which the first is a strict subset of the second, with nothing marking the nesting — a reader can take 8 and 45 as disjoint and add them. The paper is explicit about non-additivity everywhere else it states two screen counts together.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json summary gives n_designs_with_a_fully_paired_offtarget_duplex = 8 and n_designs_with_a_gap_paired_near_match_within_2_kcal = 45, both reproduced. Walking the 190 per-design records: the 8 designs with max_run_len_hybridisable == 16 (two at TAF15_e12, one at TAF15_e14, three at TFG_e2, two at TFG_e7) all carry min_ddg_any_hybridisable = 0.000 by construction, so every one of them is inside 2 kcal/mol; the 8 are a subset of the 45 and the disjoint remainder is 37, not 45. Compare the same paragraph's own handling of the mature and precursor screens two sentences earlier — 'As a union rather than a sum the two screens condemn 93 of the 190' (re-derived: |87 ∪ 19| = 93, intersection 13) — and the Discussion's 'Neither restates the other, and their counts may not be added'. The energy pair is the one place in the paper where a nested pair of counts is written as a coordinate list.
p2s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any rewording that keeps the two numbers adjacent without the nesting marker regenerates the ambiguity, and a future correction that recomputes only one of the two (for example re-running the energy screen at a different ddG cut) would leave 8 and 45 looking like independently sourced figures rather than a class and its superset. Nothing computes '45 minus 8' anywhere, so no artifact would go stale to signal the drift.
